mcq.q: The best case running time T(n) is:
mcq.e: Best case = time when the best possible thing happens (minimum).

mcq.q: The worst case running time T(n) is:
o: Always equal to the best case
mcq.e: Worst case = maximum.

mcq.q: Why do we study the functions of time complexity?
o: To know whether the algorithm becomes reasonably or incredibly slow as the problem grows
To count the lines of code
mcq.e: Growth with n is what matters.

mcq.q: Loop: i <- 1; LOOP (i <= n) { i <- i + 1 }. Its T(n) is:
mcq.e: Lines: 1 + (n + 1) + n = 2n + 2, a linear function.

mcq.q: Loop: i <- 1; LOOP (i <= n) { ...; i <- i * 2 }. How many times does the body run?
mcq.e: Doubling: 2^k = n gives k = log2(n).

mcq.q: T(n) = 6 log2(n) + 2 is which kind of function?
mcq.e: Grows with log n.

mcq.q: A linear outer loop containing a doubling inner loop gives:
mcq.e: n x log n.

mcq.q: Two nested loops, each running n times, give T(n) =
mcq.e: Inner body runs n x n times.

mcq.q: Which ordering from slowest-growing to fastest-growing is correct?
mcq.e: 1 < log n < n < n log n < n^2 < 2^n < n!.

mcq.q: Which function grows fastest?
mcq.e: Exponential beats any polynomial for large n.

mcq.q: n! (factorial) typically arises when an algorithm:
o: Tries every ordering of n items
mcq.e: There are n! permutations of n items.

mcq.q: Asymptotic notation expresses running time as its growth rate by:
o: Dropping less significant terms and constant coefficients
mcq.e: That is its definition.

mcq.q: In T(n) = 3n^2 + 50n + 200, for large n which term dominates?
mcq.e: For n > 53, n^2 > 50n + 200, so the n^2 term dominates.

mcq.q: Big-O is the asymptotic notation for the:
mcq.e: It gives an upper bound on the worst case.

o: T(n) >= c f(n) for all n >= n0
T(n) <= c f(n) for all n >= n0
T(n) = c f(n) for all n
T(n) <= c f(n) for all n <= n0

mcq.e: mid = 3 (12) then mid = 5 (23): two iterations.

written.q: Explain best case, worst case and average case running times.
written.a: Best case: the time taken when the best possible thing happens; T(n) is the minimum over n. Worst case: the time when the worst possible thing happens; T(n) is the maximum over n. Average case: the time for some probability distribution of the instance characteristic; T(n) is the average over n. Example: sequential search is 1 comparison at best, n at worst and (n + 1)/2 on average.

written.q: Determine T(n) for a loop i ← 1; LOOP (i <= n) ... i ← i * 2 whose body has 4 instructions, and say which function type it is.
written.a: The counter doubles: after k passes i = 2k, so the loop runs log2(n) times (2maxIterations = n). Lines: 1 (init) + (log n + 1) (test) + 4 log n (instructions) + log n (i ← i * 2) = 6 log2(n) + 2. It is a logarithmic function.

written.q: Define asymptotic notation and show that 3n<sup>2</sup> + 50n + 200 grows like n<sup>2</sup>.
written.a: Asymptotic notation expresses running time as a growth rate by dropping the less significant terms and constant coefficients. For n ≥ 20, 3n2 ≥ 50n + 200 (n = 20: 1200 = 1200), and for n ≥ 54, n2 ≥ 50n + 200 (n = 54: 2916 ≥ 2900). Also (50n + 200)/(3n2) → 0 as n → ∞. So the lower terms and the coefficient do not matter: growth rate n2.

written.q: State the definition of Big-O and prove that T(n) = 10n<sup>2</sup> + 4n + 2 is O(n<sup>2</sup>).
written.a:
Definition: for T(n) ≥ 0 and f(n) ≥ 0, T(n) = O(f(n)) if there exist positive constants c and n0 such that T(n) ≤ c f(n) for all n ≥ n0.

Proof: 10n2 + 4n + 2 ≤ 10n2 + 5n for n ≥ 2 (since 2 ≤ n); 10n2 + 5n ≤ 10n2 + n2 = 11n2 for n ≥ 5 (since 5n ≤ n2). So T(n) ≤ 11n2 with c = 11, n0 = 5, hence T(n) = O(n2).

written.q: Compare sequential search and binary search (requirements, worst case, trace for finding 23 in {2, 5, 8, 12, 16, 23, 38}).
written.a: Sequential search works on an unordered list and checks elements one by one: worst case n comparisons, O(n). Binary search needs a sorted list and halves the range each time: worst case about log2(n) + 1 iterations, O(log n). Trace for 23: first = 0, last = 6, mid = 3 (12): 23 > 12 so first = 4; mid = 5 (23): found, return 5.

written.q: Trace selection sort on {64, 25, 12, 22, 11} and give its time complexity.
written.a: i = 0: smallest 11, swap → 11, 25, 12, 22, 64. i = 1: smallest 12, swap → 11, 12, 25, 22, 64. i = 2: smallest 22, swap → 11, 12, 22, 25, 64. i = 3: 25 already in place. Comparisons: (n − 1) + ... + 1 = n(n − 1)/2 = 10 for n = 5, always: O(n2) in all cases; n − 1 swaps.

written.q: Trace bubble sort on {5, 1, 4, 2, 8} and give its time complexity.
written.a: Pass 1: (5,1) swap, (5,4) swap, (5,2) swap, (5,8) no → 1, 4, 2, 5, 8. Pass 2: (1,4) no, (4,2) swap, (4,5) no → 1, 2, 4, 5, 8. Pass 3: no swaps. Pass 4: no swaps. Comparisons 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 = n(n − 1)/2, so O(n2).
